What actually blocked the mint was upheld and fixed on this branch (312b24f): a spec-amend session had renumbered the spec's declared Stories from S-34950..S-34953 to S-70904..S-70907 (docs/specs/f-0148.md's own P21), but the plan's four Task headers and two Decisions-table rows (PD5, PD6) were never updated to match, re-verified directly against both files in this checkout. Since check_doc's and phantom_stories' id scans read the whole prose of the plan, not just its Task headers, those stale ids -- naming no heading anywhere in the current tree -- are exactly the kind of citation the F-0285 guard in _mint refuses the whole plan over, which also explains why no Task has minted yet (the hold's own "Writes: (none declared)"). Fixed: every stale S-34950..S-34953 citation in docs/plans/f-0148.md is now S-70904..S-70907, matching the spec's `## Stories` section id for id. Also corrected in the same commit: PD6 independently claimed `asf.record.plan_tasks.STORY_ID_RE` is `\bS-\d{4}\b` and so could never match a five-digit id -- re-read at asf/record/plan_tasks.py:29,35 and asf/record/core.py:45, the regex is built from `ID_DIGITS = r'\d{4,}'` (four or more digits), so that claim was false on this checkout and is corrected rather than left to mislead a future reader. Nothing else about the spec or plan's design was in dispute, and no finding from a formal review round applies: docs/reviews/1-f-0148.md does not exist on this branch and none was quoted in the adjudication brief. This ends the SPEC-AMEND cycle for F-0148: no further spec-amend round is needed or should be attempted -- the next tick's plan-tasks stage mints the four Story cards and the four Task cards from the (now-consistent) landed spec and plan on its own.

text: Disputed: whether a fourth spec-amend session on F-0279 could end the NO STORIES -> SPEC-AMEND loop. It cannot, and none should run. I read docs/specs/f-0279.md myself: its frontmatter already carries stories: [S-74454, S-74455, S-74456], and its `## Stories` section already declares all three under their own `### S-nnnnn:` headings with checkbox acceptance lines, matching the `## Acceptance tests` blocks one-for-one -- exactly the shape asf.record.idcheck.declared_stories and plan_tasks._mint read. A fourth spec-amend session would reproduce the third's text verbatim. Overruled: there is no further edit for a spec-amend session to make, now or on any later round -- this is not a defect in the spec. The real block is structural, and I verified it by reading the code, not by taking either side's word for it: asf.feeder.rows.needs_stories (rows.py:428) refuses any plan session for a Feature until the record holds an open Story child (has_stories, rows.py:423); but asf.record.plan_tasks._mint only turns a spec's declared `### S-nnnnn:` headings into Story cards for a Feature whose plan is already on the trunk (the `candidates` collection at plan_tasks.py:137-152 requires plan_ref(fev), and only then is specs[fid] populated for the declared-Stories read at plan_tasks.py:192-213). A cloud session has no record reach to mint a Story card directly (asf new story) the way CHANGELOG.md:749's spec-amend design normally does, and the fallback it takes instead -- declaring Stories as spec text -- only pays off once a plan lands, which the gate refuses until a Story exists: no session launched on this card, cloud or otherwise, can close that circle by itself. That is a one-time operator decision, not a question that should cycle through more sessions, so I am not filing it as another needs-input; I name the two ways out and recommend one. Recommended: an operator runs `asf new story --parent F-0279 --title <title> --acceptance <lines>` on the record host, once per Story, using the three blocks already under docs/specs/f-0279.md's `## Stories` section verbatim for title and acceptance text -- this touches only F-0279. Because `asf new` assigns the next free id from whatever block is live at call time rather than S-74454/55/56, the spec's `## Stories` and frontmatter `stories:` list must then be re-pointed at the ids it prints, in a short, ordinary spec-amend commit, before any plan session starts -- otherwise plan_tasks._mint would later read the old S-74454/55/56 as still-undeclared and mint three more Story cards on top of the real ones. The alternative -- setting conventions.feeder.stories_before_plan: false for this product so the first plan can be drafted and land, minting the three declared Stories through the designed path (F-0285) with no id to re-point -- is simpler to execute but drops the stories-first gate for every other Feature in the product, not just this one; I don't recommend it unless the operator judges that product-wide exposure acceptable.
